_meta.note: Engine data for the Assignment Compass tool. State income tax specs (2025 tax year), mandatory worker payroll deductions, local-tax flags, MERIC cost-of-living category indexes, and blind-spot cards. Every number here feeds an ESTIMATE. Keyed by stateAbbr per DATA.md.
_meta.colSource: MERIC Cost of Living Index (C2ER participation data), Q1 2026
_meta.taxSources: State revenue departments + Tax Foundation 2025 bracket tables, authored 2026-08. Brackets for states that index annually may lag one cycle.

AL.name: Alabama

notes: Standard deduction shrinks at higher incomes; max shown.

AL.local: Some cities levy occupational taxes (Birmingham 1%). Check the city, not just the state.

spots.b: Wind and hurricane deductibles on the coast run separate from the base policy. Inland Alabama is cheap to insure; Mobile is not. Quote a real address.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.noTax: No state income tax and no statewide sales tax. Some boroughs and cities levy local sales tax.

spots.b: Groceries, parts, furniture: it all rides a barge or a plane before you buy it. Budget the freight premium, and expect 2 to 6 week waits on anything you cannot buy in town.
Heating season is long and electric rates off the road system can triple Anchorage rates. Ask what the LAST tenant paid in January, not the annual average.
Phoenix cooling season runs May through October and summer electric bills routinely triple winter ones. APS and SRP both use time-of-use and demand plans that punish 5 to 8 pm usage.

notes: Simplified from the AR rate tables; top rate 3.9% for 2025.
Brackets indexed annually; personal exemption credit applied.
Mental Health Services surtax adds 1% over $1M.

payroll.label: CA SDI
payroll.note: State Disability Insurance. 1.2%, no wage cap since 2024. This comes out of every paycheck.

spots.b: In WUI zip codes carriers have pulled out and the FAIR Plan fallback costs 2 to 4x a normal policy. The state index cannot see this. Quote a real address before you commit to housing.

spots.t: Fuel is its own budget line
spots.b: California gas runs $1.30 to $1.60 over the national average. A 30-mile commute here is not the same expense it was at home.

notes: Taxed on federal taxable income. TABOR refunds have temporarily lowered the rate in some years.

payroll.label: CO FAMLI
payroll.note: Paid family leave premium, worker half of 0.9%.

spots.b: The Front Range is the most hail-battered metro corridor in the country. Home and auto premiums have climbed double digits for years. Get real quotes.
The state housing index is a Front Range number. Summit, Eagle, Pitkin, Routt: resort-county rents can double it.

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction; it phases out at higher incomes.

payroll.label: CT Paid Leave
payroll.note: 0.5% payroll deduction for the state paid leave program.

spots.b: Eversource and UI residential rates are among the highest in the continental US. Budget utilities off the index here, not off what you paid in a cheap-power state.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.local: Wilmington levies a 1.25% city wage tax.

spots.b: DC's index is driven almost entirely by rent. Everything else is near-normal expensive; housing is nearly double. The commute-from-Maryland-or-Virginia math changes your tax state too.

FL.name: Florida
FL.noTax: No state income tax. The state makes it back on sales tax, tourist taxes, and the insurance market you are about to meet.

spots.b: Highest homeowners premiums in the nation, hurricane deductibles that run 2 to 10% of dwelling value, and carriers that non-renew mid-year. Renters and auto are climbing too. Quote a real address BEFORE you sign a contract.
Statewide numbers blend Panhandle affordability with Miami. Coastal metro rent and insurance can run 30% over the state figure.

notes: Rate on a legislated glide path down; 5.19% for 2025.
2024 reform is phasing in bigger deductions and wider brackets through 2031; figures approximate the 2025 step.

payroll.label: HI TDI
payroll.note: Temporary Disability Insurance, up to 0.5% of weekly wages, capped.

spots.b: Oil-fired generation puts HECO residential rates around triple the national average. A/C habits from the mainland will hurt here.
Groceries and goods carry ocean freight in the price. The index captures some of it; specialty items and anything bulky cost more than the index suggests.

notes: Cut to 5.3% for 2025.

spots.t: Boise is not the state index
spots.b: Ada and Canyon County housing runs well above the statewide number after a decade of in-migration. Rural Idaho pulls the average down. Price the actual metro.

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction.

spots.t: Property tax rides in the rent
spots.b: Second-highest effective property tax in the country. You will not write the check as a renter, but your landlord already did.

IN.name: Indiana

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction.

IN.local: EVERY Indiana county levies its own income tax, 0.5% to 3%. This is not optional and not modeled here. Look up the county rate before you compare offers.

notes: Flat 3.8% since 2025.

KY.name: Kentucky

notes: Rate drops to 3.5% in 2026.

KY.local: Most cities and counties levy occupational license taxes on wages (Louisville 1.45%, Lexington 2.25%). Not modeled; check the locality.

notes: Flat 3% since 2025.

spots.t: Insurance crisis, second only to Florida
spots.b: Homeowners premiums have doubled in parts of the state and auto insurance is among the priciest anywhere. South of I-10, quote insurance before you commit.
Most Maine homes heat with oil or propane, delivered by truck, paid in lumps. A cold snap is a $600 fill-up. Ask how the unit heats before you sign a lease.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.local: Every Maryland county (and Baltimore City) adds a MANDATORY local income tax of 2.25% to 3.2% on top of the state rate. That is real money and it is not in this estimate. Check the county rate.

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction. 4% surtax over roughly $1.08M.

payroll.label: MA PFML
payroll.note: Worker share of Paid Family and Medical Leave.

spots.b: Greater Boston rent is the second-highest index in the lower 48 on this table. Travel stipends built for national averages do not stretch here; run the numbers before taking a Boston contract at a national rate.

MI.name: Michigan

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction.

MI.local: About two dozen cities levy income taxes; Detroit is 2.4% for residents.

spots.b: Michigan's no-fault system still produces some of the highest auto premiums in the country, especially in Detroit zip codes. Quote your actual address.

notes: First $10K exempt; 4.4% above for 2025, headed to 4% in 2026.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.local: Kansas City and St. Louis each levy a 1% earnings tax on people who live or work in the city.

spots.b: Bozeman, Missoula, Whitefish, the Flathead: in-migration pushed rents far past the state number. A Kalispell assignment does not cost what the Montana index says.

notes: Top rate on a glide path down; 5.2% for 2025.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.noTax: No state income tax. Sales tax and gaming revenue carry the state.

spots.b: Cooling a Las Vegas apartment July through September is a real budget line. NV Energy summer rates plus 110-degree heat: ask for actual summer bills.
Las Vegas premiums are well above national norms. Quote before you go.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.noTax: No tax on wages, and the interest-and-dividends tax ended in 2025. The state runs on property taxes instead.

spots.b: Among the highest property taxes in the country, and landlords pass it through. The no-income-tax win is partly priced into housing.

notes: NJ has no standard deduction; the $1,000 personal exemption is modeled as one.

spots.b: Highest property taxes in the nation (in your rent), and if you commute the Parkway, Turnpike, or a Hudson crossing, tolls are a three-figure monthly line.

notes: 2025 restructured brackets.

NY.name: New York
NY.local: New York City adds 3.078% to 3.876% city income tax for residents; Yonkers adds a surcharge. Living in NYC and working anywhere still means city tax.

spots.b: The state index averages NYC against upstate. An assignment in Buffalo or Syracuse costs FAR less than the index; the five boroughs cost far more. Weight accordingly.

notes: Rate on a glide path down; 4.25% for 2025.
Most wage earners owe zero; the first bracket is 0%.

OH.name: Ohio

notes: Personal exemption modeled as a deduction; flattening toward 2.75% by 2026.

OH.local: Nearly every Ohio municipality levies its own income tax, typically 1% to 3%, and it applies where you WORK. This is material and not modeled. Look up the city rate.

spots.b: Cheapest housing in the country, but tornado-alley insurance partially claws it back. Home and auto premiums run well above what the price of the house suggests.

OR.name: Oregon

notes: Oregon allows a federal tax subtraction (capped) that softens this a bit; not modeled.

payroll.label: Paid Leave OR
payroll.note: Worker share of the paid leave program.

OR.local: Portland-area extras for higher earners: Metro homeless services tax and Multnomah preschool tax kick in above $125K single.

spots.t: No sales tax, high everything else
spots.b: The sticker price is the price at the register, but income tax starts near 7% almost immediately and gas plus housing run well above average. The trade is not free money.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.local: Almost every PA municipality levies a local Earned Income Tax, commonly around 1%; Philadelphia's wage tax is about 3.75% for residents. Material and not modeled.

payroll.label: RI TDI
payroll.note: Temporary Disability Insurance, 1.3% up to the wage base.

notes: Top rate on a glide path down; 6.2% for 2025.

spots.b: Charleston and the coast carry separate wind and hail coverage through the state wind pool. Inland SC is cheap to insure; the Lowcountry is not.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.noTax: No state income tax. Sales tax applies to nearly everything, including groceries.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.noTax: No state income tax. Combined state and local sales tax is the highest in the country, near 9.6%, and it applies to groceries.

TX.name: Texas
TX.noTax: No state income tax. Property taxes among the highest in the nation carry the load, and renters pay them through rent.

spots.b: In most Texas metros you pick your own retail power plan, and the teaser-rate plans bite. Summer bills in a badly chosen plan can double. Read the fact label; avoid variable wholesale plans.
Hail, wind, and coastal exposure have pushed Texas premiums to the national top tier. Quote a real address.

notes: Utah uses a taxpayer credit instead of a deduction; it phases out as income rises.

spots.b: Salt Lake, Utah, and Davis County rents run above the state index after years of growth. Cheap-Utah instincts are a decade old.
Fuel oil and propane heat, delivered and paid in lumps, plus winter tires and higher rural mileage. Ask what January actually costs.
The DC suburbs price like DC; the rest of Virginia prices like the index. Same state tax return, very different rent.

WA.name: Washington

payroll.label: WA PFML
payroll.note: Worker share of Paid Family and Medical Leave.

payroll.label: WA Cares
payroll.note: Long-term care payroll tax, no cap. Together with PFML this takes over 1.2% of gross despite the no-income-tax headline.

WA.noTax: No state income tax on wages, but see the payroll deductions: WA Cares plus PFML take over 1.2% of gross, and sales tax runs over 10% in Seattle.

spots.b: Highest transportation index in the lower 48 here: top-tier gas taxes, ferries if you live across the water, and Seattle traffic mileage. Budget the commute for real.

spots.t: Seattle is not the state index
spots.b: King County housing runs far above the state number; Spokane runs below it. Price the actual metro.

notes: Personal exemptions modeled as a deduction; rates stepping down under the 2023 cuts.
The WI standard deduction phases out with income; max shown.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.noTax: No state income tax, low sales tax. The catch is what a mountain-west housing market did to the few towns people actually move to.

spots.b: Jackson prices like Aspen; Casper prices like Kansas. The state index is an average of places that share nothing but a flag.
